title: Kapsam:
summary: This text is from Turkey's Higher Education Law (Law No. 2547, dated 4/11/1981, published in the Official Gazette on 6/11/1981). It presents the First Chapter covering the law's purpose, scope, and definitions. Article 1 states the law's purpose: to establish higher education principles and to regulate in a unified manner the organization, operations, duties, authorities, and responsibilities of all higher education institutions and their superior bodies, including education, research, publication, teaching staff, students, and other personnel. Article 2 defines the scope, covering all higher education superior bodies, institutions, affiliated units, and related activities. It also notes that special legal provisions for institutions under the Ministry of National Defense and Ministry of Interior are reserved (amended by KHK-694/44 on 15/8/2017, confirmed by Law 7078/41 on 1/2/2018).

title: Tanımlar: Madde 3 – (Değişik: 17/8/1983 - 2880/1 md.)
summary: This text is Article 3 of a Turkish Higher Education Law, providing definitions for key terms. It defines: higher education (post-secondary education of at least four semesters); upper institutions (YÖK and University Council); higher education institutions (universities, high technology institutes, faculties, institutes, colleges, conservatories, research centers, and vocational colleges); high technology institute (public legal entity focused on technology research and education); university (autonomous institution with faculties and research units); faculty; institute (postgraduate education in related fields); college (vocational-focused); conservatory (music and performing arts); vocational college (two-year, pre-licensure); application and research center; department (grouping of related academic fields); teaching staff (professors, teaching assistants, research assistants); academic ranks (professor, associate professor, doctoral teaching member); and teaching assistant. One item was repealed in 2018.

title: p) (Mülga: 22/2/2018-7100/2 md.)
summary: The text defines key higher education terms in Turkish law: Associate Degree (2+ year program based on secondary education), Bachelor's (8+ semesters), and Postgraduate levels including Master's (research-based, post-bachelor's), Doctorate (6+ semesters post-bachelor's or 4+ post-master's, original research), Medical Specialization, Artistic Proficiency (original artistic work, doctoral-level equivalent), and Veterinary Specialization. It also defines four higher education types: Regular (mandatory attendance), Open (via radio/TV), External (exam-only with optional evening classes), and Continuing Education (community-wide skill development). Additionally, it defines Vocational and Technical Education Regions (linking vocational colleges with secondary institutions) and Post-Doctoral Research (up to 3 years of research experience within 7 years after completing a doctorate or specialization). The text concludes with the heading for the Second Chapter: General Provisions.

title: Amaç:
summary: Article 4 defines the purpose of higher education in three parts: (a) cultivating students who are loyal to Atatürk's principles and Turkish nationalism, embody Turkish cultural and moral values, prioritize public good over personal interest, fulfill civic duties to the Turkish Republic, possess free scientific thinking, broad worldview, and respect for human rights, develop balanced physical, mental, and moral health, and acquire professional knowledge and skills for national development and personal livelihood; (b) contributing to Turkey's economic, social, and cultural development as an indivisible whole, aiming to make the nation a constructive, creative, and distinguished partner of contemporary civilization; and (c) conducting high-level scientific research, producing knowledge and technology, disseminating scientific data, supporting national development, collaborating with domestic and international institutions, and contributing to universal and contemporary progress.

title: Ana ilkeler:
summary: The text covers Article 5 (Basic Principles of Higher Education) and Article 6 (Council of Higher Education) of Turkey's Higher Education Law. Article 5 outlines nine principles: instilling Atatürk's principles and service consciousness; preserving national culture and unity; ensuring educational unity; planning curricula based on scientific and national needs; guaranteeing equal opportunity; establishing universities by law and vocational schools by presidential decision; developing and distributing higher education nationwide; and mandating courses (Atatürk Principles, Turkish, foreign language, occupational safety for specific faculties, and optional PE/arts) for at least two semesters. Article 6 defines the Council of Higher Education as an autonomous body with legal personality overseeing all higher education. It details the Council's 21-member composition (selected by the President and Inter-University Council), its organs (General Assembly, President, Executive Council), meeting quorums, voting rules, salary regulations, continuous duty requirements, employment restrictions for members, and exemption from age limits.

title: Yükseköğretim Kurulunun görevleri: Madde 7 – (Değişik: 17/8/1983 - 2880/3 md.)
summary: Article 7 of the Higher Education Law (amended 1983, further modified by KHK 703 in 2018) defines the duties of the Higher Education Council (YÖK). These include: (a) preparing short- and long-term plans for establishing, developing, and operating higher education institutions, training academic staff domestically and abroad, and monitoring the effective use of allocated university resources; (b) ensuring harmonious cooperation and coordination among higher education institutions; (c) determining growth limits for universities and implementing measures such as summer, night, and dual teaching to maintain efficiency; and (d) within the framework of state development plans, making decisions on opening, merging, or closing faculties, institutes, colleges, departments, research centers, conservatories, and vocational colleges, as well as suspending or resuming education when disruptions occur. A footnote notes that references to the 'Council of Ministers' in items (d) and (e) were changed to 'the President' by KHK 703 (2018), and item (d)(1) was repealed.

title: (3) (Mülga: 2/7/2018 – KHK-703/135 md.)
summary: The text outlines the duties of a Turkish higher education governing body (YÖK), covering: specialization of higher education institutions; determining minimum course hours, transfer rules, and continuation education criteria; setting professor, associate professor, and doctoral teaching staff quotas based on institutional needs; reviewing annual activity reports and identifying top/underperforming institutions; determining student capacity and admission criteria; ensuring equality of opportunity in admissions; deciding on tuition fees; reviewing and approving budgets for submission to the Ministry of National Education; handling rectors' disciplinary matters and severing ties with non-compliant teaching staff; establishing scientific national committees; assigning developed universities to support newer ones; providing opinions on foundation-established institutions; determining equivalence of foreign diplomas; and performing other legally assigned duties. A repealed provision and a legislative amendment note are also included.

title: Yükseköğretim Denetleme Kurulu: Madde 8 –
summary: Article 8 defines the Higher Education Supervisory Board (Yükseköğretim Denetleme Kurulu) as a YÖK-affiliated body overseeing universities, their units, teaching staff, and activities. It details the Board's composition: 15 members from professors and experienced ministry inspectors, 3 from judicial/accounting bodies, and 1 each from the Ministries of National Defense and National Education. Appointments follow standard procedures, with the President appointed by the YÖK President. Members serve 3-year terms, are separated from their institutions, and face the same age limits as teaching staff. Re-election is permitted; early departures trigger replacement for the remaining term. Salaries are set by the President, capped at YÖK member levels, with retired members retaining pensions. Members are barred from other employment except temporary assignments. Those absent over 3 months (excluding annual leave) per year are deemed to have left. Public institutions may second inspectors and experts to the Board for up to 2 years upon YÖK's request, with paid leave status and service credit.

title: Yükseköğretim Denetleme Kurulunun görevleri: Madde 9 – (Değişik: 17/8/1983 - 2880/5 md.)
summary: The text covers two articles from Turkish higher education law. Article 9 defines the duties of the Higher Education Supervisory Board: supervising compliance of educational activities with legal principles, conducting investigations requested by the YÖK President, and performing other assigned tasks. A footnote notes the replacement of 'Council of Ministers' with 'President.' Article 10 addresses fund transfers: 25% of ÖSYM's annual budget surplus is transferred to YÖK by end of February. YÖK may allocate this as own revenue and budget items. The funds are prioritized for scientific research projects, domestic/international faculty and student exchange programs, training of professors and researchers, and strengthening YÖK's infrastructure. Payments to institutions are made via special accounts. Students in exchange programs may receive scholarships up to three times the standard amount, and faculty may receive up to ten times the additional lesson fee. All program expenses are covered from special accounts. Procedures are set jointly by the Ministry of Finance and YÖK, with expenditures audited under Law 5018.

title: Üniversitelerarası Kurul: Madde 11 –
summary: Article 11 of the Inter-University Council law covers its establishment, operation, and duties. The council comprises university rectors and one professor per university (selected by senates for four years). Rectors chair for one year based on founding dates. An 11-member Management Board (from science, health, social sciences, and fine arts) is established, meeting monthly, with authority to handle delegated duties. The council can form permanent/temporary commissions for domestic and international cooperation, meets at least twice yearly, and its agenda is sent to relevant authorities. The Minister of Education and YÖK Chair may attend. As an academic body, its duties include: coordinating education, research, and publication; proposing faculty/staff measures; preparing regulations; ensuring harmony among similar faculties; determining doctoral standards and evaluating foreign degrees; forming juries for associate professorship evaluations; and performing other legally assigned tasks. A 2018 amendment removed the General Staff's professor selection provision.

title: DÖRDÜNCÜ BÖLÜM
summary: This text is from the Fourth Chapter of a Turkish higher education law, specifically Article 12, which outlines the duties of higher education institutions. These duties include: (a) conducting education, research, publication, and consultancy aligned with contemporary civilization and national development plans; (b) training human resources efficiently in needed fields; (c) disseminating scientific knowledge to raise living standards and inform public opinion; (d) providing formal, widespread, continuous, and open education, particularly in industrialization and agricultural modernization; (e) addressing scientific, cultural, social, and economic issues in cooperation with other institutions and advising public bodies; (f) supporting institutions delivering various education services; (g) contributing to regional agriculture and industry development, professional training, modernization, production growth, and environmental solutions; (h) producing, developing, and disseminating educational technology; and (ı) developing applied higher education principles and operating revolving fund enterprises. A footnote references additional articles regarding foundations establishing higher education institutions. The text ends with a heading for 'University Organs.'

title: Rektör: Madde 13 –
summary: Article 13 defines the Rector's appointment, duties, and responsibilities. Rectors of state and foundation universities are appointed by the President; in foundation universities, based on the board of trustees' proposal. The rector represents the university's legal entity. The age limit is 67, though incumbents may serve until term end (a Constitutional Court annulment takes effect June 2025). The rector selects up to three vice-rectors from salaried professors (up to five in open-education universities), limited to their term. A vice-rector acts as deputy during absence; YÖK must be notified if absence exceeds two weeks, and a new rector is appointed if the deputy period exceeds six months. The rector's duties include: presiding over university councils and implementing higher-education decisions; reporting education, research, and publication activities to the Inter-University Council; preparing investment programs, budgets, and staffing plans for YÖK; reassigning or assigning new duties to staff; exercising general supervision over all units and personnel; and performing other statutory duties. The rector holds primary authority and responsibility for rational use of teaching capacity, student social services, security, planning activities per state development goals, and scientific/administrative oversight, including delegation to sub-units.

title: Senato: Madde 14 –
summary: Article 14 defines the Senate's composition, operation, and duties. The Senate comprises the rector, vice-rectors, deans, one elected faculty member per faculty (three-year term), and directors of attached institutes and colleges. It meets at least twice yearly (beginning and end of academic year), with the rector able to convene additional sessions. As the university's academic organ, its duties include: deciding on education, research, and publication principles; preparing or commenting on university-wide draft laws and regulations; drafting regulations for official publication after rector's approval; approving the annual academic program and calendar; granting honorary academic titles and deciding on faculty board proposals; reviewing objections to faculty and institute/college board decisions; selecting university administrative board members; and performing other legally assigned tasks.

title: Üniversite Yönetim Kurulu: Madde 15 –
summary: The text covers Article 15 on the University Management Council. It addresses: (a) Composition and operation – the council is chaired by the rector, includes deans and three professors elected by the senate for four years to represent various teaching units; the rector convenes meetings; vice-rectors may attend without voting rights. (b) Duties – the council assists the rector in administrative activities by: (1) helping implement higher education body and senate decisions; (2) ensuring activity plan implementation, reviewing investment programs and budget drafts considering unit proposals, and submitting them to the rector or board of trustees (for foundation universities); (3) deciding on university management matters raised by the rector; (4) reviewing and finalizing objections to faculty, institute, and college council decisions; (5) performing other legally assigned duties. The text concludes with a heading for Faculty Organs.

title: Dekan: Madde 16 –
summary: This text defines the Dean's appointment, duties, and responsibilities. The dean, representing the faculty, is selected by the Higher Education Council from three professors proposed by the rector for a three-year term, with reappointment possible. The dean appoints up to two vice deans (up to four in open-education universities) for a maximum of three years; a vice dean acts as deputy in the dean's absence, and if this exceeds six months, a new dean is appointed. The dean's duties include presiding over faculty boards, implementing their decisions, reporting the faculty's status to the rector annually and upon request, submitting budget and staffing proposals, and exercising general supervision over all faculty units and personnel. The dean bears first-degree responsibility to the rector for rational use of teaching capacity, security, student social services, education, research, publication activities, and overall supervision and control of all faculty operations.

title: Fakülte Kurulu: Madde 17 –
summary: Article 17 defines the Faculty Council's composition, operation, and duties. The council is chaired by the dean and includes department heads, institute/college directors (if applicable), three professors elected by professors, two associate professors elected by associate professors, and one doctoral teaching member elected by doctoral teaching members, all serving three-year terms. It meets at the start and end of each semester, with the dean able to convene additional meetings. As an academic body, its duties include: (1) determining the faculty's education, research, and publication activities, related regulations, plans, programs, and academic calendar; (2) selecting members of the faculty management board; and (3) performing other duties assigned by law.

title: Fakülte Yönetim Kurulu: Madde 18 –
summary: Article 18 defines the Faculty Management Board's composition, operation, and duties. The board consists of the dean (chair), three professors, two associate professors, and one doctoral teaching member, selected by the faculty council for three years. It convenes at the dean's call and may establish temporary working groups or education-coordination offices. As an administrative support organ to the dean, its duties include: assisting in implementing faculty council decisions; ensuring education, planning, programs, and calendar execution; preparing investment, program, and budget proposals; deciding on all faculty management matters brought by the dean; ruling on student admission, course transfers, dismissals, and exam procedures; and performing other legally assigned tasks. Footnotes note a 2018 legal amendment replacing 'assistant associate professor' with 'doctoral teaching member.' The text ends with a heading for 'Institutes.'

title: Organlar: Madde 19 –
summary: Article 19 defines the organs of an institute: the institute director, institute council, and institute management board. The director is appointed by the rector for three years based on the faculty dean's recommendation (or directly by the rector for rectorate-affiliated institutes), can be reappointed, and appoints up to two deputies from salaried academic staff. Deputieship or vacancy procedures mirror those for deans. The director performs duties assigned to deans for the institute. The institute council comprises the director (chair), deputies, and chairpersons of the main scientific fields. The management board includes the director (chair), deputies, and three professors selected by the council for three years from six candidates nominated by the director. Both the council and management board carry out the duties assigned to the faculty council and faculty management board, respectively, for the institute. The text also introduces the topic of Higher Schools (Yüksekokullar).

title: Organlar: Madde 20 –
summary: The text covers Turkish higher education law provisions on institutional governance. Article 20 defines higher school organs (director, board, management committee), their appointment procedures (3-year terms, reappointment allowed), composition, and duties mirroring those of deans and faculty bodies. Article 21 regulates departments: prohibits duplicate departments, specifies department head appointment from professors/associate professors/doctoral teaching members for 3 years, deputy appointment for absences, replacement after 6+ months absence, and the head's responsibility for education, research, and departmental activities. Article 22 outlines teaching staff duties: conducting education at associate degree, bachelor's, and graduate levels, managing projects and seminars, and performing scientific research and publications. A footnote notes a 2018 amendment replacing 'assistant associate professors' with 'doctoral teaching members.'

title: Bölüm:
summary: The text covers Turkish higher education regulations on: (1) School (yüksekokul) director's deputies, acting procedures, and council/management board composition and duties; (2) Department (bölüm) governance, including head appointment criteria, term, reappointment, and deputy rules; (3) Teaching staff duties (education, research, student guidance, assigned tasks); (4) Doctoral teaching member (doktor öğretim üyesi) appointment process, qualifications, and additional conditions; (5) Associate professorship (doçentlik) requirements (degree, language exam, publications), jury evaluation process, and appointment procedures; (6) Professorship promotion requirements (5 years post-doçent, original publications) and appointment via a five-professor panel; (7) Recognition of foreign associate professorship and professorship titles in Turkey, requiring at least two years of work abroad and YÖK approval.

title: Professor Appointment Rules and Foreign Academic Title Recognition
key_items: Yabancı ülkelerde alınan doçentlik ünvanı: Madde 27 – (Değişik: 17/8/1983 - 2880/12 md.)
Yabancı ülkelerde alınan profesörlük ünvanı: Madde 28 – (Değişik: 17/8/1983 - 2880/13 md.)
summary: The text covers requirements and procedures for professor appointments in Turkish universities, including the need for original publications after obtaining docent title, designation of a main research work, and the possibility of additional quality-based conditions approved by YÖK. It details the appointment process: positions announced by the rector, evaluation by a panel of five professors (at least three from other institutions) who write individual reports and express preferences, followed by the rector's appointment decision. It also states that a professor appointed to one institution can only transfer to another by following the same procedures. Articles 27 and 28 address recognition of foreign docent and professor titles in Turkey: candidates must hold a PhD or specialization, have obtained the foreign title, and worked at least two years in foreign teaching/research institutions. Recognition requires a University Council decision confirming the foreign institution is equivalent to Turkish higher education institutions.

title: Protection of Academic Titles and Retirement Age for Teaching Members
summary: Article 29 protects academic titles of teaching members, prohibiting their deprivation except as legally specified. Departing members may retain titles, but those holding professor, associate professor, or doctoral titles must serve two years in higher education per title period to use them externally. Article 30 sets the retirement age at 67. An additional provision allows institutions to retain valuable teaching members on one-year contracts up to age 75, with YÖK approval. Their compensation is capped at the net amount of their last position's indicators, bonuses, and allowances after deductions. Their insurance status continues under their previous title, and standard prohibitions, duties, responsibilities, and disciplinary rules apply. Procedures are determined by YÖK with Ministry of Finance consent.

title: Öğretim görevlileri: Madde 31 – (Değişik: 17/8/1983 - 2880/14 md.)
summary: Article 31 of the Turkish Higher Education Law defines the appointment and employment of teaching staff (öğretim görevlileri). Key points: (1) They may be appointed for courses lacking a full teaching member or for specialized topics, based on recognized expertise, on a temporary or hourly-rate basis. (2) Candidates for teaching staff positions must hold at least a thesis-based master's degree, except for YÖK-designated specialized fields in vocational schools. (3) Appointment requires opinions from administrative boards, suggestions from deans or department heads, and rector approval. (4) They can be placed in teaching member, research assistant, or teaching staff positions, or employed without a position on hourly/contract basis. (5) Teaching staff may be appointed to teaching member positions for a maximum of two years, renewable if no other candidate applies and continuation is deemed beneficial. (6) Duties end automatically upon expiration; reappointment follows the initial procedure. (7) Conservatories and vocational schools may appoint permanent teaching staff as needed. A 2018 amendment replaced 'yardımcı doçentlik' with 'doktor öğretim üyesi.'

title: Okutmanlar: Madde 32 – (Mülga: 22/2/2018-7100/6 md.)
summary: The text covers Turkish higher education personnel regulations (Articles 32-34). Article 32 on lecturers was repealed in 2018. Article 33 defines research assistants as teaching staff assisting in research and experiments, requiring applicants to be under 35, appointed for up to three years with rector approval, and reappointable. It details financial provisions for research assistants sent abroad for graduate education, including 60% net salary retention, additional payments under Law 1416, scholarship top-ups, and biannual book/stationery allowances. Subsections b-e were repealed in 2018. Article 34 addresses foreign-national teaching staff, appointed by the rector with faculty and university council recommendations, subject to the same salary rules as domestic staff. Their appointment requires YÖK pre-approval and a work permit from the Ministry of Labor. Their number is capped at 2% of filled teaching positions, with YÖK managing distribution, contracts, and renewals.

title: Öğretim elemanı yetiştirme:
summary: The text covers Turkish Higher Education Law provisions on teaching staff training and working principles. It includes amendments to staff training approval procedures (YÖK pre-approval, Ministry of Labor work permits, presidential authority) and a Constitutional Court annulment. Article 35 addresses domestic/international training of teaching staff per development plans and YÖK needs, temporary allocation of research assistant positions, and mandatory service obligations. Article 36 details working principles: permanent status, copyright fees, minimum weekly teaching hours (10 for professors, 12 for teaching assistants), exemptions for administrative roles, YÖK-determined equivalences for non-class activities, contractual employment of professors/associate professors in medical/dental faculties (salary caps, contract limits, administrative restrictions), medical staff working in private hospitals (50% cap, performance criteria, penalties), and hospital hiring limits (20% cap). Article 37 permits external entities to request scientific services, research, and patient care from universities, with fees credited to revolving funds.

title: Kamu kuruluşları ve vakıflarda görevlendirme: 36
summary: Article 38 governs the temporary assignment of academic staff to public institutions, professional organizations, associations, and foundations. Assignment requires the institution's request, the staff member's consent, university board approval, and the rector's approval, with personnel matters remaining with the home institution. Assigned staff retain their salary and rights at their home university but cannot benefit from revolving funds (except those assigned to YÖK, its units, the Inter-University Council, or the Forensic Medicine Institute). No separate assignment decision is needed for roles in management or supervisory boards of professional organizations, associations, or foundations, provided academic duties are not disrupted. Universities may also serve as official expert witnesses in forensic medicine cases. Assigned staff receive an additional second-duty salary capped at the equivalent of a first-degree, fourth-rank general manager's salary, determined by the relevant minister. These payments need not be deposited to revolving funds, and no further payments are made by the assigned institution.

title: Yurt içinde ve yurt dışında görevlendirme: Madde 39 – (Değişik: 9/4/1990 - KHK - 418/25 md.; İptal: Anayasa Mahkemesinin 5/2/1992 tarihli ve E.1990/22, K.1992/6 sayılı Kararı ile; Yeniden düzenleme: 18/5/1994 - KHK - 527/17 md.)
summary: Article 39 governs domestic and international assignments of academic staff. It permits deans (up to 1 week) and rectors (up to 15 days) to authorize attendance at conferences, seminars, and research trips without travel allowance. Longer or costlier assignments require management board and rector approval. Academic staff may be sent abroad for training, education, or internships within presidentially set quotas (max 1 year) or via external scholarships, subject to university management board and rector decisions. Extensions up to half the duration are allowed in necessary cases. Staff are subject to Law 657 provisions for civil servants sent abroad, though payments may be set lower. Those receiving foreign scholarships may be granted paid or unpaid leave. Travel allowances follow civil servant equivalents, paid from university or relevant institution budgets. Additionally, academic staff invited by institutions in Turkish Republics and related communities may receive paid leave up to 3 years (5 years for internationally established universities) with ministry approval.

title: Kurumlararası yardımlaşma: 38
summary: Article 40 on inter-institutional cooperation in Turkish higher education covers: (a) Teaching staff unable to fill their weekly teaching load may be assigned by the rector to other units or institutions in the same city; no extra fee is paid within their load, but extra fees are paid from the host institution's budget for work exceeding it. (b) Teaching staff may be assigned to another university for at least one academic year upon request, personal willingness, board opinions, rector's proposal, and YÖK approval; their positions are reserved for five years; priority in appointments goes to those with at least five years of service in developing regions; assignments to foundation universities are capped at two years with no administrative duties. (c) Teaching needs of National Defense University, Gendarmerie/Coast Guard Academy, and Police-affiliated institutions are met by other local institutions upon named requests. (d) If no local staff is available, those assigned from other cities receive temporary travel allowance and double extra teaching fees.

title: Öğretim üyesi ihtiyacının karşılanması: Madde 41 – (Değişik: 17/8/1983 - 2880/22 md.)
summary: Article 41 of the Turkish Higher Education Law governs the fulfillment of teaching staff needs in state higher education institutions. The Higher Education Council (YÖK) determines staff requirements across various disciplines and assigns them to relevant universities, considering existing faculty. Assignments last between one and four semesters, with positions retained at the home university. A 2011 Constitutional Court decision annulled one sentence. A 2018 amendment updated terminology (e.g., 'teaching assistants' to 'teaching staff'; 'Turkish Armed Forces' to 'National Defense University, Gendarmerie and Coast Guard Academy'). Civil servant rules apply to notification, resignation, notice periods, and commencement. Assignment decisions must specify duration. Personnel rights continue at the home institution, while allowances and temporary duty travel expenses (per Law 6245) are paid from the host university's budget. Those who fail to start within the legal deadline are deemed to have resigned and cannot be reassigned to any higher education institution or other public institution until the service obligation is fulfilled.

title: Bilimsel denetim:
key_items: Diploma alma, ders kredilerinin hesaplanması, öğrencilik haklarından yararlanma
summary: The text covers Turkish higher education law provisions: (1) Article 42 on internal scientific supervision of academic staff, including annual reporting chains (department head→dean→rector→YÖK) and publication archiving; (2) Article 43 on undergraduate education structure, equivalence standards, teaching methods, and international joint programs; (3) Article 44 on diploma requirements, credit calculation, maximum study durations (4-9 years depending on program), preparatory year rules, exam rights for failing students, electronic and distance education, and advisory boards; (4) Article 45 on admission via central exams, high school score weighting, special quotas for top graduates, vocational graduates, vertical transfers, foreign students, and talented/competition-winning students; (5) Article 46 on current service cost calculation, student contribution fees and tuition structures, payment deadlines, scholarships, part-time student work, revenue allocation for student services, and education support for vocational colleges in industrial zones.

title: Sosyal hizmetler:
summary: The text covers two articles from Turkish higher education law. Article 47 addresses social services: higher education institutions must protect students' physical and mental health and meet social needs (housing, nutrition, leisure) by providing facilities such as reading rooms, health centers, canteens, sports halls, and camp sites. They must also cooperate with organizations to help graduates find employment, establish guidance and psychological counseling centers for personal/family issues, and manage public-institution scholarships distributed by YÖK based on state development plans, covering tuition, lab, exam, and diploma fees. Article 48 governs the printing and reproduction of textbooks and educational materials: universities or YÖK prepare and sell textbooks, computer/electronic materials, and distance education content at appropriate prices. Teaching staff cannot independently print or reproduce teaching materials; these must be handled by the university, except when the university's board confirms in writing that printing is impossible within the academic year. Rules and copyright fees are set by YÖK with Ministry of Finance approval.

title: Yabancı dil hazırlık eğitim - öğretimi:
summary:
Yabancı dil hazırlık eğitim - öğretimi:
Madde 49 – Eğitim - öğretimini kısmen veya tamamen bir yabancı dilden yapan Yükseköğretim Kurumları, kaydını yaptıran öğrencileri, öğrenimde kullanılacak yabancı dilde bir yeterlilik sınavına tabi tutarlar. Yetersiz bulunan öğrenciler için esasları Yükseköğretim Kurulunca tespit edilecek, bir yıla kadar süreli, bir yabancı dil hazırlık öğrenimi uygulanır.

title: (Mülga son cümle: 19/11/2014-6569/33 md.) (...)
key_items: SEKİZİNCİ BÖLÜM Memurlar ve Diğer Görevliler
summary: The text covers Turkish higher education regulations, including: (1) a note on a repealed sentence; (2) the requirement for institutions to continuously develop students' foreign language skills during regular education; (3) Article 50 on postgraduate education, detailing: selection of master's, veterinary specialization, doctoral, and medical specialization candidates via exams and Inter-University Board criteria; institutional planning obligations for postgraduate programs; a repealed clause; eligibility of postgraduate students for scholarships and one-year research assistant appointments; and salary determinations for medical specialization students referencing Ministry of Health personnel pay; (4) footnotes documenting legislative amendments (2001, 2014, 2018) to the article's title, content, and terminology; and (5) a reference to Section 8 covering Civil Servants and Other Officials.

title: Yönetim örgütleri: Madde 51 –
summary: Article 51 defines administrative organizations in higher education institutions. It specifies that umbrella organizations have a general secretary under the president, and universities have one under the rector, overseeing central administration with department heads, directors, advisors, legal advisors, experts, and civil servants (per Law No. 657). Departments and directorates are established by board decisions. Each faculty has a secretary under the dean; institutes and high schools have secretaries under their directors, supported by sufficient staff for office and internal services, with division of labor approved by the dean or director. General secretaries and secretaries serve as rapporteurs in their institution's boards without voting rights.

title: Atamalar:
key_items: DOKUZUNCU BÖLÜM Disiplin ve Ceza İşleri
summary: Article 52 of the Turkish Higher Education Law outlines appointment principles for various positions. It specifies that general secretaries, department heads, directors, legal advisors, and specialists are appointed by heads of upper institutions or rectors, with appropriate consultations. Faculty, institute, and college secretaries are appointed by rectors based on dean or director proposals. Education requirements are set: general secretaries need a bachelor's degree, while faculty/institute/college secretaries need a higher education diploma. Civil servant appointments are made by heads or rectors based on proposals from deans, directors, or general secretaries, using cadre as reference. Auxiliary service staff appointments follow similar proposal-based procedures at different institutional levels. A 2011 amendment removed the 'Student Selection and Placement Center President' reference. Monthly or contractual management positions are determined by heads or rectors and proposed to relevant authorities. Transfers of civil servants and other officials between public institutions or higher education institutions are made based on proposals from general secretaries, rectors, or the Higher Education Council President. The text concludes with the heading for the Ninth Section on Discipline and Penalty Matters.

title: Genel esaslar: Madde 53 –
summary: Article 53 of Turkish higher education law defines disciplinary authority and penalties. It establishes who serves as disciplinary authority (YÖK President, rectors, deans, institute directors, etc.) for various levels of academic institutions. It lists six disciplinary penalties for teaching staff: warning, reprimand, salary deduction, suspension of grade advancement, removal from teaching profession, and removal from public service. Non-teaching staff fall under Labor Law or Civil Servants Law. The text details specific acts warranting a warning (negligence in training subordinates, not acknowledging research support, improper complaints) and a reprimand (giving private lessons, unauthorized use of institutional spaces, violating patient rights, biomedical research violations, unauthorized sharing of unpublished work, publishing survey data without consent, lacking research permits, violating international treaties, failing to warn about harmful practices, distributing hate materials, political activities in universities, verbal disrespect to superiors, and misuse of official equipment).

title: Reprimand Penalty for Academic Staff: Definition and Offenses
summary: The text defines 'Kınama' (reprimand) as a written notification to academic staff of fault in duties and behavior. It enumerates acts warranting this penalty: giving private lessons to enrolled students; using university premises without permission for non-service purposes; disregarding patient rights in publications; violating regulations in biomedical/clinical research; sharing unpublished work without author consent; publishing survey data without participant consent or institutional permission; failing to obtain required research permits; violating regulations or international treaties in research; failing to warn about harmful practices; distributing violence or hate materials; conducting political party activities in universities; fault in performing duties; failing to fulfill notification obligations; verbal disrespect toward superiors; and misusing, losing, or damaging official equipment. Items a, c, and l were repealed by Law 7243 (15/4/2020), while items o, p, r, and s were added by the same law. Footnotes detail specific textual amendments made by this legislation.

summary: The text covers disciplinary penalties and criminal investigation procedures for Turkish higher education institution staff. It lists offenses warranting: (u) repeated unauthorized absence from mandatory meetings; (3) salary/wage deduction (1/30–1/8) for acts like unauthorized disclosure of institutional decisions, failure to return institutional property, animal/ecological harm, data misuse, improper use of research resources, predatory publication, authorship manipulation, false accusations, unauthorized system access, misleading academic claims, intentional neglect of duties, unauthorized absence (3–9 days), unauthorized use of premises, and distribution of prohibited publications; (4) grade progression suspension or multiple wage deductions for document forgery, corruption, obstruction of services, interference with teaching, false statements via media, research data fabrication, discrimination, duplicate publications, intoxication at work, false reports, unauthorized trade, confidentiality breaches, and threats; (5) dismissal from teaching profession for plagiarism, use of others' work, and 20-day unauthorized absence; (6) dismissal from public service for terrorism, assault/sexual harassment, disgraceful conduct, drug offenses, and data crimes. It also details criminal investigation procedures, including initial and final investigation stages, competent decision-making bodies by rank, quorum rules, appeal mechanisms, jurisdiction, and exceptions where prosecutors act directly.

title: Disiplin soruşturması ve savunma hakkı: Madde 53/A- (Ek: 2/12/2016 - 6764/27 md.)
summary: The text covers Article 53/A on disciplinary investigation procedures and defense rights in Turkish higher education law. It outlines: initiation of investigation by the disciplinary officer; prohibition of duplicate investigations; mandatory scientific ethics committee review before investigation; investigator appointment and rank requirements; rules for joint offenses and position changes; investigator's powers (collecting evidence, hearing witnesses, expert consultation); document submission obligations; scope limitations; record-keeping; confidentiality; two-month completion deadline with extension provisions; investigation continuing after retirement; non-interference of criminal proceedings and administrative sanctions; and defense rights including the right to examine documents, hear witnesses, and make oral/written defense for severe penalties. Some defense provisions were annulled by the Constitutional Court (2022). Amendments by Law 7243 (2020) updated legal references.

title: Görevden uzaklaştırma: Madde 53/B- (Ek: 2/12/2016 - 6764/28 md.)
summary: The text defines 'görevden uzaklaştırma' (suspension from duty) as a precautionary measure applicable to administrators, teaching staff, civil servants, and other personnel in state or foundation higher education institutions. It can be imposed for three months at any stage of disciplinary or criminal investigation and extended in three-month increments. The investigation must begin within ten working days. Authorized decision-makers include Higher Education Senior Body Presidents, authorized superiors, rectors, and directors; rectors, deans, and independent college directors require a Higher Education General Assembly decision. Suspended personnel retain social rights and receive two-thirds of their salary; the withheld one-third is paid upon reinstatement, and the suspension period counts toward career progression in state institutions. Officials acting arbitrarily or failing to initiate investigation face legal, financial, and criminal liability. The measure is immediately lifted if dismissal from public service is not recommended, if other penalties are imposed, or if the investigation is pardoned. It may also be removed early if the person's presence does not hinder the investigation.

title: Zamanaşımı: Madde 53/C- (Ek: 2/12/2016 - 6764/29 md.)
summary: This text covers the statute of limitations (Zamanaşımı) for disciplinary punishments under Article 53/C. It specifies: (1) Investigation initiation deadlines—1 month for warning, reprimand, salary deduction, and grade advancement suspension; 6 months for removal from university teaching or public service—counted from when the act is discovered. (2) Punishment imposition deadlines—2 years from the act's commission, or 6 years for acts warranting removal from university teaching. (3) The statute of limitations restarts if a scientific work is used in academic appointments/promotions or republished in whole or part. (4) If a court annuls a disciplinary punishment, a new one may be imposed within the remaining limitation period, or within 3 months if less than 3 months remain, considering the court's reasoning.

title: Disiplin cezası verme yetkisi: Madde 53/Ç- (Ek: 2/12/2016 - 6764/30 md.)
summary: The text outlines Article 53/Ç on disciplinary punishment authority. It specifies which officials and committees can impose different levels of punishment: (a) warnings and reprimands by hierarchical officers or the Higher Education Council President for rectors/directors; (b) salary deductions and grade suspensions by unit disciplinary committees; (c) removal from teaching or public service by the High Disciplinary Council upon the appointing officer's proposal; (d) all punishments for rectors, directors, and deans by the High Disciplinary Council. It notes a sentence struck down by the Constitutional Court. Authorities may return files for deficiencies, accept, reduce, or reject proposed punishments, with a three-month deadline for new action after rejection. The authority is non-delegable. Disciplinary committees may examine personnel files, obtain information, conduct investigations, hear witnesses and experts, and perform inspections.

title: Disiplin cezası verilmesinde uygulanacak temel ilkeler: Madde 53/D- (Ek: 2/12/2016 - 6764/31 md.)
summary: Article 53/D outlines fundamental principles for applying disciplinary penalties: no multiple penalties for the same act (heaviest applies if multiple offenses); recidivism within the removal period triggers a one-degree heavier penalty (requiring a finalized penalty); three same-degree penalties for separate acts also escalate one degree; pardoned and recidivism-based penalties are excluded from recidivism calculations; positive service records or awards allow a one-degree lighter penalty; the penalty hierarchy links dismissal from public service as the upper limit and grade suspension/salary deduction as the lower limit; similar acts receive equivalent penalties; if grade suspension is inapplicable (last grade), salary deduction (1/4 to 1/2) applies, with recidivism leading to dismissal. Penalties take effect immediately or the following month. Notifications go to higher authorities, the university, and the State Personnel Presidency. Recipients face 3-5 year appointment restrictions to senior academic/administrative positions, and incumbents in such roles are automatically removed.

title: Disiplin kurullarının teşekkülü: Madde 53/E- (Ek: 2/12/2016 - 6764/32 md.)
summary: The text outlines the formation of disciplinary boards in Turkish higher education. The High Disciplinary Board is the Higher Education General Assembly. University disciplinary boards are the university management boards, while unit management boards serve as disciplinary boards for their units. For Rectorate-attached units, academic staff cases are handled by a board chaired by a vice rector with four professors; civil servant cases by a board chaired by the General Secretary with the Legal Advisor and Personnel Department Head. YÖK staff cases are handled by a board chaired by the General Secretary with the 1st Legal Advisor and relevant department heads. Inter-University Council staff cases are handled by a board chaired by the General Secretary with the Deputy General Secretary and Legal Advisor. Exclusion rules prevent members from voting on cases involving their own rank or themselves. Investigators cannot vote in disciplinary boards, and board members cannot vote in appeal proceedings. Vacancies are filled by equivalent-rank teaching members selected by the senate. A footnote notes the term 'assistant professors' was replaced with 'doctoral teaching members' by Law 7100 (2018).

title: Disciplinary Objections, File Storage, and Student Disciplinary Penalties
summary: The text covers three sections of Turkish higher education disciplinary regulations. Article 53/F details objection procedures to disciplinary penalties: which authorities handle objections for warnings, reprimands, salary deductions, and grade suspensions; the 7-day objection deadline; the 60-day decision period; and consequences of accepted or rejected objections, including the possibility of new actions within three months. Article 53/G addresses storage of disciplinary penalties in personnel files, specifying that warnings and reprimands may be removed after five years and salary deductions or grade suspensions after ten years, upon request and if the individual's conduct justifies it. Article 54 begins student disciplinary matters, listing penalties and offenses, starting with reprimand (kınama) and its triggering actions such as providing misleading information to authorities and disrupting academic activities like courses, seminars, exams, and laboratories.

title: 3) (İptal alt bent: Anayasa Mahkemesinin 22/2/2024 tarihli ve E: 2023/78, K: 2024/55 sayılı Kararı ile)
summary: The text outlines Turkish higher education disciplinary regulations, covering: (1) specific offenses warranting reprimand, suspension (1 week–1 month, 1 semester, 2 semesters), or expulsion, including cheating, vandalism, threats, drug use, weapons, sexual harassment, plagiarism, and organizational crimes; (2) recidivism rules (one degree heavier penalty, but no expulsion for repeat offenses); (3) disciplinary authorities (deans, rectors) and their jurisdiction; (4) investigation timelines (30 days, extendable to 60/90 days) and statute of limitations (1–3 months to initiate, 2 years to impose); (5) student's right to defense (7-day notice, oral/written); (6) investigation procedures (confidentiality, witnesses, reports); (7) penalty-imposing authorities and disciplinary committee procedures; (8) voting rules, decision timelines (10 days), and mitigation options; (9) notification, 15-day appeal to university board, and judicial recourse; (10) service of notices and file management. Several sub-clauses were annulled by the Constitutional Court (22/2/2024).

title: Mali kolaylıklar: Madde 56 – (Değişik: 17/8/1983 - 2880/30 md.)
summary: Article 56 outlines financial facilities for higher education institutions in Turkey. It covers: (a) tax, fee, and stamp duty exemptions for donations and bequests to higher education bodies, with donor conditions respected; (b) universities and high technology institutes receiving the same financial exemptions as general budget public institutions, plus tax-deductible donations by taxpayers to qualifying universities and foundations; (c) customs and tax exemptions for imported equipment, materials, and publications used in education and research not available domestically; (d) authority of rectors and higher education heads to waive rights up to 1 million lira, with Ministry of Finance approval required above that; (e) exemption of research and publication expenses from tender law (Law 2490); (f) exemption of construction, equipment, and maintenance from General Accounting Law and tender law; (g) inter-university budget transfer authority vested in the Minister of Finance with YÖK's proposal.

title: İta amirliği, mali denetim:
summary: The text covers two articles from Turkish higher education law. Article 57 addresses financial oversight: budgets of higher education institutions are prepared, implemented, and audited per general and special budget principles. The budget officer is the president in upper institutions and the rector in universities, with authority delegable to deputies, deans, institute directors, unit heads, and general secretaries. In foundation universities, the board of trustees chairman serves as budget officer. Article 58 covers revolving capital: it can be established with university management council proposal and YÖK approval. Initial capital may be funded from the institution's budget. Revenues are tracked separately by units. Capital can be increased by management council decision, funded from year-end profits. Once paid capital reaches the allocated amount, remaining profits are added to the following year's revenue. Revenue sources include goods and services sales and other income.

title: (Mülga altıncı paragraf: 2/1/2014-6514/12 md.)
summary: This text outlines Turkish higher education revolving fund (döner sermaye) regulations covering: (1) fund usage for continuous services, high-cost medical devices, and multi-year commitments; (2) minimum allocation percentages by institution type (35% medical/dental, 30% agriculture/veterinary, 15% others) for purchases, maintenance, and manager shares; (3) at least 5% for scientific research project financing with advance payment provisions; (4) detailed additional payment (ek ödeme) rates for medical/dental faculty staff, other personnel, and specialized units based on contribution levels; (5) manager shares for rectors, deans, and hospital directors with specific percentage caps; (6) after-hours service payments and international health service revenue distribution; (7) university-industry cooperation revenue allocation (85% to staff); (8) general principles requiring economic efficiency and revenue-expenditure balance; (9) minimum payment guarantees tied to civil servant pay scales; and (10) regulatory authority vested in YÖK with Ministry of Finance approval.

title: ONBİRİNCİ BÖLÜM
summary: Chapter 11 (Various Provisions) of the Higher Education Law covers: (1) Political party membership: teaching staff may join parties and serve in party central organs/research units but cannot hold YÖK, rector, dean, or department head positions; students may join parties; neither may conduct party activities or propaganda on campus. (2) Return to institutions: those who served as VP, minister, or legislator; voluntarily departed teaching staff (except court/disciplinary removals); and those who completed terms as YÖK members, rectors, or deans may return to their universities without position requirements, with seniority credited. (3) Voting: no abstention allowed; quorum is majority of members; decisions by simple majority; plurality applies in a fourth round if no majority is reached. (4) Personnel rights: governed by this law, then University Personnel Law, then general provisions. (5) Records: maintained per general rules and YÖK regulations; used for appointments, promotions, and academic titles. (6) Leave: annual leave for teaching staff during academic breaks.

title: Higher Education Law: Return, Voting, Personnel Rights, and Records
summary: The page covers four topics from a Turkish higher education law. First, rules for returning to higher education institutions: retired faculty who return keep their pensions; voluntary leavers (except those dismissed by court/disciplinary action) may return without vacancy requirements; those who served in YÖK, YÖK Denetleme Kurulu, rector, or dean positions and left after completing their term return with seniority and salary adjustments. Second, voting (Art. 61): board members must vote accept or reject (no abstention); quorum is a majority of members; decisions require simple majority of attendees; if no majority in the third round, plurality applies in the fourth. Third, personnel rights (Art. 62): faculty and staff rights follow this law, then the University Personnel Law, then general provisions. Fourth, records (Art. 63): records of faculty, staff, and students are kept per general rules and YÖK regulations, and serve as the basis for appointments, promotions, and academic titles.

title: İzinler:
summary: Article 64 outlines leave regulations for academic staff in Turkish higher education. Teaching staff use annual leave during standard academic breaks. Other leave types for teaching staff, as well as leave matters for higher education upper institutions' personnel and university civil servants, are governed by the Civil Servants Law (No. 657). A legislative amendment note indicates that references to the 'Council of Ministers' were replaced with 'Vice Presidency, Ministry' via KHK 703 (2/7/2018). Rectors must obtain annual leave and foreign travel permissions from the YÖK (Higher Education Council) President, while other managers obtain them from their immediate superior. All personnel in higher education institutions and upper bodies may leave their post only with authorization from their first disciplinary superior.

summary: This text is from Turkey's Higher Education Law, listing matters (items 3-14) to be regulated by regulations issued by the Council of Higher Education (YÖK), including: doctoral teaching membership and promotion processes, teaching staff training, weekly teaching loads, foreign student fees, textbook printing and copyright, disciplinary procedures for staff and students, scientific research and maintenance expenses, personnel records, foundation university requirements, assignment/transfer rules, and scientific research ethics boards. It also specifies that graduate education principles and other academic matters are regulated by the Inter-University Council. Finally, Article 66 repeals the old University Law (No. 1750) and conflicting provisions of numerous university-specific laws (e.g., Istanbul Technical, Karadeniz Technical, Ege, Atatürk, METU, Hacettepe, Diyarbakır, Çukurova, Anadolu, Cumhuriyet, İnönü, Boğaziçi, Ankara, Istanbul, and Kayseri universities).

title: Ek Madde 1 – (Ek: 14/4/1982-2653/6 md.)
summary:
Ek Madde 1 – (Ek: 14/4/1982-2653/6 md.)
Üniversite rektörleri, fakülte dekanları, enstitü ve yüksekokul müdürleri ile bunların yardımcıları ve bölüm başkanları, gerektiğinde bu Kanunda belirtilen süreleri dolmadan tayinlerindeki usule uygun olarak görevlerinden alınabilirler.

title: Ek Madde 2 – (Ek: 17/8/1983 - 2880/32 md.; Değişik : 18/6/2008-5772/7 md.)
summary: This text is Article 2 (Ek Madde 2) of a Turkish higher education law (originally 1983, amended 2008). It stipulates that foundations may establish vocational colleges (meslek yüksekokulu) provided they are non-profit, comply with academic, faculty, and security standards set by the law, and aim to train high-quality workforce in economically needed fields. The college may be established as part of a higher education institution or independently, without being attached to a university or high technology institute. The vocational college holds public legal personality and is established by Presidential decision. Its establishment is conditional upon demonstrated need within the relevant vocational and technical education region.

title: Ek Madde 3 – (Ek: 17/8/1983 - 2880/32 md.)
summary: The text covers supplementary articles (Ek Madde 3-8) of a Turkish higher education law regarding foundation (vakıf) universities. Ek Madde 3 lists required documents for establishing a foundation university, including proof of facilities, 20% annual operating cost coverage, unit names, commitment documents, and specific requirements for medical faculties (200-bed hospital, YÖK standards, Health Ministry compliance). Ek Madde 4 prohibits foundations from establishing military or security education institutions. Ek Madde 5 mandates a board of trustees (mütevelli heyeti) of at least 7 members with civil servant qualifications, 2/3 holding bachelor's degrees, elected for 4-year terms, responsible for representing the institution, appointing managers with YÖK approval, approving budgets, and managing personnel. Ek Madde 6 grants the institution separate legal personality, prohibiting revenue transfer to the foundation. Ek Madde 7 provides tax exemptions and financial benefits, while prohibiting real estate acquisition via expropriation. Ek Madde 8 references a Constitutional Court decision's effective date.

title: Foundation Higher Education Institutions: Governance and Legal Status
summary: The page covers supplementary articles (Ek Madde 4–7) of a Turkish higher education law regarding foundation-established institutions. Ek Madde 4 prohibits foundations from opening military or security education institutions. Ek Madde 5 mandates a board of trustees (mütevelli heyeti) of at least seven members, elected for four years, with civil-servant qualifications and at least two-thirds holding a bachelor's degree; the board represents the institution's legal personality, appoints managers with YÖK approval, handles staffing contracts, approves the budget, and monitors operations. Ek Madde 6 grants the institution a separate legal personality distinct from the foundation, prohibits transfer of its revenues to foundation assets, and allows direct donations. Ek Madde 7 extends Article 56 financial facilities, tax exemptions, and property-tax relief to foundation institutions, and a 2013 addition bars them from acquiring real estate via expropriation. A prior article's cancellation by the Constitutional Court (1992) is also noted.

title: Ek Madde 8 – (Ek: 17/8/1983 - 2880/32 md.)
summary: The text covers Additional Articles 8 and 9 of a Turkish higher education law regarding foundation (vakıf) universities. Article 8 states that the Constitutional Court decision took effect one year after its 9/2/1991 Official Gazette publication. It mandates that academic organs, teaching staff qualifications, and duties in foundation institutions mirror those in state institutions. Persons banned or dismissed from state institutions cannot work in foundation ones. A 2020 amendment requires foundation institutions to pay teaching staff no less than equivalent state salaries, calculated based on position-linked payments. Article 9 establishes that foundation institutions' education principles, teaching durations, and student rights are governed by this Law, with student fees set by the board of trustees. A 2020 amendment obligates foundation institutions to provide free education to at least 15% of students with the highest central placement scores in each program level (associate, bachelor's, thesis master's, doctoral), with no fees charged. For thesis master's, doctoral, and special-talent programs, highest placement score ranking applies. The Higher Education Council (YÖK) determines implementation procedures.

title: Ek Madde 10 – (Ek: 17/8/1983 - 2880/32 md.)
summary: This text is Additional Article 10 of a Turkish higher education law. It stipulates that foundation-established higher education institutions must submit their annual reports to the Higher Education Council (YÖK) at the end of each academic year, similar to state institutions, and are subject to YÖK's supervision in financial, administrative, and economic matters. An additional paragraph (2018) grants YÖK the authority to request information, documents, or inspections from related parties regarding goods/services transactions or financial movements. It defines 'related parties' as the founding foundation, board members, managers, and any individuals or institutions directly or indirectly connected to them in management, supervision, or capital, including spouses, direct relatives up to the third degree, and in-laws. A further paragraph allows YÖK to request oversight of these institutions' foreign financial and financial relations from relevant public institutions.

title: Ek Madde 11 – (Ek: 17/8/1983 - 2880/32 md.)
summary: The text covers Ek Madde 11-15 of Turkey's Higher Education Law regarding foundation (vakıf) higher education institutions. Ek Madde 11 details: suspension of institutions with inadequate education; penalties for resource transfers to foundations/third parties; revocation of activity permits by Presidential decision; student transfer to guarantor/state universities with continued fee payment; liquidation under Civil Code with YÖK and Finance Ministry oversight; tax exemptions; liquidator liability limits; protection from seizures/enforcement during liquidation; remaining assets returning to the foundation; board/manager positions ending automatically; personnel governed by Labor Law; temporary suspension procedures with trustee appointment; and YÖK's regulatory authority. Ek Madde 12 grants foundation institutions' academic councils, senates, boards, and rectors equivalent authority to state counterparts. Ek Madde 13 is repealed. Ek Madde 14 assigns YÖK authority over education areas, facilities, staffing, and procurement regulations. Ek Madde 15 ensures institutional continuity if the founding foundation dissolves, with assets transferring to the institution and board selection authority passing to another foundation.

title: Foundation Higher Education Institutions: YÖK Authority and Governance Provisions
summary: The text covers legal provisions governing foundation (vakıf) higher education institutions in Turkey. It includes: YÖK's authority to determine tuition fees, manage student transfers, and ensure uninterrupted operations; YÖK's power to resolve implementation doubts by consulting the Finance and National Education ministries; supervision procedures and corrective, restrictive, or license-removal measures for foundation institutions; Additional Article 12, stating that academic councils, senates, management boards, and rectors in foundation institutions exercise equivalent powers to their public counterparts; Additional Article 13, which was repealed in 1991; and Additional Article 14, specifying that YÖK determines education areas, facilities, equipment, teaching and management staff, and other academic matters, as well as regulations governing sales, leasing, procurement, and construction activities of foundation institutions.

title: Ek Madde 15 – (Ek: 17/8/1983 - 2880/32 md.)
summary: The text covers Additional Articles 15-22 of Turkey's Higher Education Law. Article 15 addresses the continuation of a foundation's higher education institution upon the foundation's dissolution, asset transfer to the institution, and transfer of governance authority to another foundation with YÖK approval. Article 16 permits open education universities to establish domestic service units, foreign centers for Turkish citizens, create or modify units, cooperate with foreign open education institutions, and convert or add regular/open education departments. Article 17 guarantees dress code freedom in higher education institutions. Articles 18, 19, 21, and 22 are repealed or annulled. Article 20 establishes Bilkent University as a public legal entity founded jointly by three Hacettepe-related foundations. The text also references various Constitutional Court decisions, legislative amendments, and repeals affecting these provisions.

title: Additional Articles on Open Education, Dress Code, and Bilkent University

summary: The page contains Additional Articles (Ek Madde 16–22) from the Turkish Higher Education Law. Ek Madde 16 regulates open education universities' authority to establish domestic service units, foreign centers for Turkish citizens, and organizational changes, requiring YÖK approval for converting regular education departments. Ek Madde 17 grants dress code freedom in higher education institutions. Ek Madde 18 was repealed in 2020. Ek Madde 19 was annulled by the Constitutional Court in 1992. Ek Madde 20 establishes Bilkent University as a public legal entity founded by three Hacettepe-related foundations, with part b) annulled by the Constitutional Court. Ek Madde 21 was repealed in 2012. Ek Madde 22 was added in 1992 and repealed in 2010.

title: Supplementary Articles on Higher Education: Internships, Vocational Training, and Real Estate Revenue
summary: The text covers three supplementary articles of a Turkish Higher Education Law. Article 23 permits practical courses and internships in public or equivalent private institutions of the student's choice, with students remaining under discipline rules. Article 24 establishes vocational-technical education regions linking vocational colleges with secondary vocational institutions to train qualified workforce, requiring at least one region per province; regulations are set by the Ministry of Education and YÖK, covering internship rules and hourly teaching fees for assigned staff. Article 25 authorizes the Finance Minister to record revenues from renting, selling, or operating registered real estate of higher education institutions, and from renting Treasury-allocated properties for educational, health, and social purposes, as special budget items; capital expenditures link to the annual investment program, unspent amounts carry over, and non-proprietary rights may be established for student dormitory construction.

title: Ek Madde 26 – (Ek: 17/9/2004 - 5234/2 md.)
summary: The text covers two additional articles (Ek Madde 26 and 27) of Turkish higher education law. Article 26 regulates summer school tuition fees at universities and high technology institutes: fees are capped at 280 lesson hours and 2x the annual student contribution, determined by YÖK. Exemptions apply to mandatory-service, scholarship, and research-assistant students. The university board may reduce or waive fees. Payments go to public bank accounts, recorded as revenue and special fund; up to 70% funds teaching staff (max 5x lesson/3x exam fees per Law 2914), the rest covers goods/services. Unspent funds roll to the next year. No supplementary payments from other sources are permitted. YÖK approval is mandatory. Article 27 governs second-education thesis-less master's programs: tuition in at least 2 installments, minimum 30% allocated to research projects, remainder as special fund for teaching staff (max 10x lesson/5x exam fees) and administrative overtime pay. Distance education may also apply. Both articles require YÖK procedures with Ministry of Finance approval.

title: Higher Education Law: Research, Intern, and ÖYP Provisions
summary: The text covers three additional articles of a Turkish Higher Education Law. Ek Madde 28 regulates scientific research project funds in higher education institutions, requiring transfer to special project accounts with procedures set jointly by the Ministry of Finance, State Planning Organization, and YÖK, subject to audit under Law 5018. Ek Madde 29 establishes intern training payments for medical and dental students in their final years, specifying amounts for state and foundation universities, granting foundation university boards authority to set higher payments, and clarifying that no employment relationship, social insurance, or tax obligations arise. Ek Madde 30 addresses the Faculty Member Training Program (ÖYP), converting research assistants' status to a specified category, removing mandatory service obligations for those not reappointed, and requiring those studying abroad or at other universities to return within 15 days or face appointment cancellation.

title: Ek Madde 31- (Ek: 17/4/2017-KHK-690/65 md.; Aynen kabul: 1/2/2018-7077/55

nodes.title: Ek Madde 31- (Ek: 17/4/2017-KHK-690/65 md.; Aynen kabul: 1/2/2018-7077/55 (intro)
nodes.summary: The text covers two additional articles of a Turkish higher education law. Ek Madde 31 (with parts annulled by the Constitutional Court in 2023) prohibits equivalence recognition of diplomas and degrees from foreign institutions linked to terrorism organizations. Ek Madde 32 establishes the framework for technology transfer offices: higher education institutions may create them as capital companies with YÖK approval for R&D, innovation, IP protection, and public-private collaboration. It specifies funding sources (research funds, revolving revenues), staffing rules (Labor Law 4857, foreign hires under Law 6735), academic staff employment (full/part-time with permission), unpaid leave provisions for full-time staff, social security premium responsibilities under Law 5510, exclusion from Public Procurement Law 2886, and that regulations are set by YÖK with input from the Science and Finance Ministries. Conflicting provisions of Article 36 are excluded.

nodes.title: Ücretli araştırma izni: Ek Madde 33- (Ek: 18/6/2017-7033/18 md.)
nodes.summary: The text covers two supplementary articles of a Turkish Higher Education Law. Article 33 (Paid Research Leave): Teaching members with six years of actual service at state higher education institutions may receive one year of paid leave for R&D work domestically or abroad, subject to faculty board opinion, service continuity measures, and university board approval of their work program. A second leave requires at least six additional years of service after the first leave ends. Article 34 (Post-doctoral Researcher Employment): Post-doctoral researchers (within seven years of doctorate, specialization, or artistic proficiency) may be contractually employed for up to three years in research centers/institutes for R&D, innovation, or design projects under Law 5746, funded from special budgets. Employment is capped at 2% of filled teaching staff positions, does not confer civil service rights, and salaries (capped at 60,000 indicator × civil servant coefficient) are set by YÖK. No additional payments are permitted. Other employment terms follow Law 657 Article 4(B) for R&D positions.

nodes.title: Yükseköğretim Kalite Güvencesi Sistemi ve Yükseköğretim Kalite Kurulu: Ek Madde 35- (Ek: 18/6/2017-7033/18 md.)
nodes.summary: The text covers four supplementary articles of Turkish higher education law. Article 35 establishes the Higher Education Quality Assurance System and the Quality Council (YÖKAK), a 13-member autonomous public body with special budget, responsible for internal/external QA, accreditation, and independent evaluation authorization. It details member composition (from YÖK, Inter-University Council, ministries, accreditation bodies, TÜBİTAK, Health Institutes, TOBB, and a student representative), qualifications (10+ years experience), terms (4 years, max 2 terms; student rep 1 year), quorum/decision rules, organizational structure (Council + General Secretariat with three units), revenue sources, staff regulations, salary equivalences, and prohibition on concurrent employment. Article 36 creates a 7-member Advisory Council for Employment-Focused Education Programs, chaired by the YÖK President, advising on new programs and quotas. Article 37 establishes a Vocational Colleges Coordination Council for setting standards, developing programs, and advising on employment and bachelor completion. Article 38 regulates research assistant appointments, allowing up to 30% of PhD/artist-qualification completers to be appointed by their institution's senate.

nodes.title: Higher Education Quality, Advisory, and Vocational Coordination Councils
key_items: Yükseköğretim Eğitim Programları Danışma Kurulu: Ek Madde 36- (Ek: 18/6/2017-7033/18 md.)
Meslek Yüksekokulları Koordinasyon Kurulu: Ek Madde 37- (Ek: 18/6/2017-7033/18 md.)
nodes.summary: The page covers three main provisions. First, it outlines the Higher Education Quality Council's authority to regulate quality assurance systems, internal/external evaluations, quality committees, certification, and General Secretariat operations via bylaws. Second, Additional Article 36 (added 18/6/2017) establishes the Higher Education Education Programs Advisory Council, chaired by the YÖK President with seven members from Science, Industry, Development, Finance, Education, Health ministries, SGK, and TOBB, tasked with advising on employment-oriented policies and new program/quota planning. Third, Additional Article 37 (added 18/6/2017) establishes the Vocational Colleges Coordination Council, chaired by the YÖK President with a selected vocational college dean and representatives from relevant ministries and TOBB, responsible for setting standards, developing programs, monitoring employment, and advising on bachelor's completion processes. Both councils' working procedures are determined by YÖK bylaws. The page ends with a reference to research assistant employment (Article 94).

nodes.title: Ek Madde 38- (Ek: 18/6/2017-7033/18 md.)
nodes.summary: Article 38 (added by Law 7033/18, effective 1/1/2018) governs appointments to research assistant positions in Turkish higher education institutions under Article 50(1)(d). Up to 30% of appointees who complete doctoral or artistic proficiency training may be promoted to doctoral teaching member positions based on YÖK-approved performance criteria. Those not promoted must work at a different institution for at least one academic year to qualify for teaching member positions. Mandatory service obligations for doctoral training periods at other domestic institutions are waived. An additional paragraph (added 2020, amended 2022) provides that research assistants completing doctoral, dental, pharmacy, veterinary, or artistic proficiency training receive a one-year position extension, renewable once if performance criteria are met, after which the position is automatically terminated. Those completing thesis-based master's programs receive up to six months to begin doctoral or artistic proficiency training at a state institution; failure to do so results in automatic termination of their position.

summary: This section covers supplementary articles (Ek Madde 31–38) of Turkish higher education law. Ek Madde 31 prohibits equivalence recognition of diplomas from foreign institutions linked to terrorism. Ek Madde 32 establishes the framework for technology transfer offices as capital companies under YÖK approval, detailing funding, staffing, social security, and procurement exclusions. Ek Madde 33 grants paid research leave (one year) to teaching members with six years of service. Ek Madde 34 regulates post-doctoral researcher contractual employment (up to three years, 2% cap, salary limits). Ek Madde 35 creates the Higher Education Quality Assurance System and the 13-member Quality Council (YÖKAK) for accreditation and evaluation. Ek Madde 36 establishes a seven-member Advisory Council for employment-focused education programs. Ek Madde 37 creates a Vocational Colleges Coordination Council for standards and program development. Ek Madde 38 governs research assistant appointments, allowing up to 30% promotion to teaching positions, with service obligations, position extensions, and termination conditions.
