key_items: Hukuk Mesleklerine Giriş Sınavı ve İdari Yargı Ön Sınavı: Ek Madde 41- (Ek:17/10/2019-7188/5 md.)
nodes.summary: The text covers three supplementary articles of Turkish higher education law. Ek Madde 39 allows state universities to establish academic units and social facilities abroad by Presidential decision, with procedures set by Presidential regulation. Ek Madde 40 mandates that postgraduate theses be made electronically accessible via YÖK's National Thesis Center unless classified. Ek Madde 41 establishes the Law Professions Entry Exam (HMG) and Administrative Judiciary Preliminary Exam (İYÖS) as prerequisites for judge/prosecutor assistant positions and lawyer/notary internships. It specifies eligibility criteria, detailed subject areas tested (including 2024 additions like International Law and Social Security Law), exam frequency (HMG at least annually, İYÖS biennially), administration by ÖSYM under a Ministry of Justice protocol, test format (multiple-choice, minimum 120 questions, 70/100 passing score), and regulatory oversight by the Ministry of Justice with input from HSK, YÖK, ÖSYM, and bar/notary associations. Footnotes document amendments from 2017–2024.

nodes.title: Ek Madde 42 – (Ek: 15/4/2020-7243/17 md.)
nodes.summary: The text covers Ek Madde 42-45 of Turkey's Higher Education Law. Ek Madde 42 requires foundation universities to annually transfer 2% of student revenue to a public bank account as a guarantee for completing students' education if the institution's permit is suspended/revoked; transfers stop when the total covers all enrolled students' graduation tuition. An unconditional bank guarantee is also acceptable. The account is monitored by Treasury and YÖK, and funds cannot be used for other purposes or claimed by creditors. Ek Madde 43 allows YÖK to establish joint R&D application/research centers within a coordinator university (max two with same mission), with procedures set by YÖK regulation. Ek Madde 44 mandates that 80% of quarterly revenue surpluses from open education revolving funds be transferred to YÖK for training doctoral researchers at state universities, with scholarships available for priority-area doctoral students. Ek Madde 45 (incomplete) addresses Treasury budget support for state university medical/dental faculties and health institutes whose revolving fund debt coverage ratios fall below a Treasury-determined threshold.

nodes.title: Higher Education Provisions on Accounts, Research Centers, and Scholarships
nodes.summary: The text covers three provisions of Turkish higher education law. First, it stipulates that when a foundation higher education institution's activity permit is suspended or revoked, accumulated account funds may only be used to complete students' education; creditors have no claim over these funds, and procedures are set by YÖK regulations with Treasury and Finance Ministry input. Second, Additional Article 43 allows YÖK to establish joint application and research centers within state institutions for R&D aligned with development plans, limited to two centers per name and mission, with procedures set by YÖK with input from three ministries. Third, Additional Article 44 mandates that open education faculty revolving fund revenues be used exclusively for their activities, with 80% of quarterly surpluses transferred to YÖK for training doctoral researchers and providing scholarships in priority areas, with procedures set by YÖK with Treasury and Strategy and Budget Presidency approval.

nodes.title: Ek Madde 45 – (Ek: 16/4/2020-7244/4 md.)
nodes.summary: Article 45 (Ek Madde 45) addresses fund transfers to state university medical and dental faculties, their affiliated health application and research centers, and rectorate-dependent health service institutes. Specifically, revolving fund units of these institutions whose debt coverage rates fall below the threshold set by the Ministry of Treasury and Finance may receive budget transfers from that Ministry. The procedures and principles governing such transfers are determined by the Ministry of Treasury and Finance in consultation with the Strategy and Budget Presidency. All related expenditures are subject to audit by the Ministry's audit personnel, who evaluate in detail whether the transferred funds are used in accordance with the established principles and for their intended purpose.

nodes.title: Ek Madde 46- (Ek: 1/7/2022-7417/33 md.)
Ek Madde 46- (Ek: 1/7/2022-7417/33 md.) (intro)
nodes.summary: The text covers Additional Article 46 and Temporary Provisions of a Turkish higher education law. Article 46 allows qualified doctoral researchers from foreign universities, R&D centers, public research institutes, technology zones, or private labs to be assigned part-time (max one year) to higher education institutions, with salary capped at a 40,000 indicator coefficient, subject to YÖK approval. Their number is limited to 2% of the institution's filled academic staff quota. They must engage in teaching, research, R&D, or design work, and assignments can be extended based on publications. The Temporary Provisions (Articles 1-7) address: dissolution and reconstitution of existing academic councils; fixed end dates for rectors (July 31, 1982) and deans/directors (August 31, 1982); YÖK establishment within three months; interim secretariat arrangements; biennial member renewal by lottery for YÖK and its Inspection Council; a nine-month deadline for reorganizing regulations; equivalence of pre-existing academic titles; and a freeze on filling vacant positions pending YÖK's new quota determinations.

nodes.title: Geçici Madde 8 – (Değişik: 27/5/1988 – 3455/1 md.)
nodes.summary: The text contains Temporary Articles 8–18 of a Turkish Higher Education Law, providing transitional provisions. Article 8 addresses applications for associate professor/professor titles under old regulations, granting full academic rights and priority appointment; it also covers TSK and Police institutions. Article 9 grants a one-year extension for incomplete associate professorship exam stages. Article 10 allows assistants in doctoral/specialty work to serve as research assistants for one year. Article 11 ensures continued salary for teaching/administrative staff, including those whose institution status changed. Article 12 permits appointment to assistant positions pending cadre laws. Article 13 protects over-time students but requires annual success. Article 14 maintains old personnel law provisions until status determination. Article 15 mandates associate professorship applications within one year for doctoral/specialty holders or dismissal. Article 16 allows non-cadre professors/associate professors to continue working. Article 17 protects METU and Boğaziçi University staff salaries during transition. Article 18 reclassifies METU assistant professors as associate professors if qualified.

nodes.title: Geçici Madde 19 – (Değişik: 24/9/1982 – 2708/1 md.)
nodes.summary: Temporary Article 19 stipulates that non-teaching personnel at Boğaziçi and Middle East Technical Universities, not subject to Civil Servants Law 657 as of November 6, 1981, are converted to civil servant status effective September 30, 1982, with salary adjustments completed by September 30, 1983, per Law 2595's criteria without written application. Until adjustments are finalized, their existing salary and benefits continue. If the new compensation package falls below their previous earnings, the difference is paid as compensation until offset by grade or degree increases. An added provision addresses personnel who qualified for old-age pensions under Law 506 by September 30, 1982, and applied to the Social Security Institution by September 30, 1983, processing them under labor law while counting interim service under Law 506 with premium payments. Temporary Article 20 sets the retirement age for teaching members at 70 (1982), 69 (1983), and 68 (1984).

nodes.title: Geçici Madde 21 – (Mülga: 27/5/1988 – 3455/3 md.)
nodes.summary:
Geçici Madde 21 – (Mülga: 27/5/1988 – 3455/3 md.)
Geçici Madde 22 – Bu kanunun yürürlüğe girdiği tarihten itibaren bir yıl içinde bu kanun kapsamına giren öğretim üyelerinin daimi veya kısmi statüde görev yapmaları konusunda tercihlerini yapmaları istenir. Tercihlerini belirtenlerin atamaları bu kanun hükümlerine göre yapılır. Tercihlerini yapamayanların kurumları ile ilişikleri kesilir.

nodes.title: Geçici Madde 23 – (Değişik: 24/9/1982 – 2708/2 md.)
nodes.summary: The text covers Temporary Articles 23-30 of a Turkish Higher Education Law. Article 23 allows retired university staff to continue in their status until September 1983. Article 24 extends existing revolving fund regulations until YÖK issues new ones. Article 25 permits METU to continue 1981 financial operations into 1982. Article 26 allocates 10-year budget funds for university dormitory construction, prioritizing developing regions. Article 27 transfers the University Student Selection and Placement Center to YÖK with all assets and personnel. Article 28 mandates YÖK review existing academies, faculties, and institutes within six months for reorganization by the 1982-83 academic year. Article 29 allows students who left between 1963-1977 to re-enroll within three months, with detailed adaptation rules, military service provisions, and exclusions for those dismissed under Law 1402, criminal convictions, or post-1981 disciplinary actions. Article 30 permits professors who relocated from universities outside Ankara, Istanbul, and Izmir to return to their previous institution within one year if a vacant position exists.

nodes.title: Geçici Madde 30 – (Ek: 10/12/1988 – 3511/3 md.)
nodes.summary: The text covers Temporary Articles 30-35 of a Turkish Higher Education Law. Article 30 grants one exam opportunity per course to students whose enrollment was terminated for non-disciplinary reasons, allowing them to resume studies within Article 44 limits; those failing up to 3 courses get an additional exam chance, and final-year students with one remaining course may take mid-year exams until end of 1992 by paying tuition. Article 31 provides one opportunity for graduate students who failed to complete required stages (course, qualification, thesis exams) within prescribed periods. Article 32 extends Article 30 provisions to those terminated from Gülhane Military Medical Academy. Article 33 requires university senates to publish the Article 44 regulation within one month. Article 34 (1989) applies Decree-Law Article 6 to research assistants abroad for graduate studies. Article 34 (1990) preserves rights of associate professors who were TBMP members. Article 35 exempts pre-law professors from the 5-year partial status restriction in Law 2547.

nodes.title: Temporary Provisions on Higher Education Exam Rights and Transitions
nodes.summary: The page covers temporary provisions (Geçici Madde 31–35) of a Turkish higher education law. It grants an additional exam right to students failing up to three courses and allows final-year students with one remaining course to take mid-year exams until end of 1992. Geçici Madde 31 gives graduate students whose records were deleted one chance to complete required stages within three months. Geçici Madde 32 extends similar rights to those severed from Gülhane Military Medical Academy. Geçici Madde 33 requires university senates to publish the Article 44 regulation within one month. Geçici Madde 34 (1989) applies Decree-Law Article 6 to research assistants abroad. Geçici Madde 34 (1990) preserves deans' rights as former TBMP members for one year. Geçici Madde 35 exempts pre-existing professors from the five-year partial-status restriction in Law 2547.

nodes.title: Temporary Provisions on Academic and Student Rights (Articles 36-39)
nodes.summary: The page contains four temporary articles (36-39) added by Law 3747/6 on 29/5/1991 to a Turkish higher education law. Article 36 grants priority professorship appointment to those who applied before 31 Dec 1989 under Law 2547's temporary provision for promotion without cadre requirement. Article 37 provides exam and make-up exam rights to students whose enrollment was terminated (non-disciplinary reasons) between 1985/1986 and the law's publication, allowing them to resume studies within Article 44 limits; it also extends rights to Gülhane Military Medical Academy students and permits students with one remaining course to sit exams until end of 1995. Article 38 grants one application right to graduate students whose records were deleted for failing to complete required stages (course, qualification, thesis exams) within prescribed periods. Article 39 waives late fees and interest for students who pay outstanding university fees within three months of the law's publication.

nodes.title: Temporary Provisions on Student Re-enrollment and Faculty Retirement
nodes.summary: The page contains three temporary articles of a Turkish Higher Education Law. Article 40 grants students whose enrollment was terminated (1980–1992) one exam and one make-up exam per failing course, or for GPA failures, one exam and one make-up exam in chosen courses; successful students resume studies within Article 44 limits, with YÖK setting adaptation rules for others. Article 41 extends the retirement age for faculty to 72 (until end of 1998) if they serve at universities or High Technology Institutes established in 1992 or later. Article 42 allows students who lost enrollment due to unpaid contribution fees (through 1992–1993) to re-enroll within three months without late fees or interest; students terminated at the end of 1991–1992 receive two exam chances; and former Gülhane Military Medical Academy students may apply within three months for placement in a medical faculty, enjoying the same rights as other students under these provisions.

nodes.title: Temporary Provisions on Student Reinstatement and Academic Part-Time Status
nodes.summary: The text covers two temporary provisions of Turkish Higher Education Law. Article 43 grants two exam rights to undergraduate and graduate students whose enrollment was terminated for any reason from 1981-1982 until the law's publication, enabling them to resume studies. It extends similar rights to graduate students who failed courses, could not complete within prescribed periods, or passed courses but missed GPA/doctoral exam requirements. Gülhane Military Medical Academy students terminated for failure from 1992-1993 may transfer to YÖK-assigned medical faculties. All applications must be filed within three months of the law's publication. Article 44 permits professors and associate professors whose part-time status requests were previously rejected to reapply within three months of the law's effective date, provided they have served five years in full-time status in that academic position at the university.

nodes.title: Geçici Madde 45 – (Ek: 14/8/1997 – 4305/1 md.)
nodes.summary: Temporary Article 45 (added 14/8/1997, Law 4305/1) addresses two groups: (1) Students at Gülhane Military Medical Academy whose enrollment was terminated from 1994-1995 onward (excluding those with pending disciplinary court cases) may apply within 3 months of the law's publication; YÖK assigns them to medical faculties where their transfer is processed, and they receive the same benefits as other students under Law 2547. (2) Students in any educational institution whose enrollment was or will be terminated (including master's and doctoral students) may apply within 2 months to the relevant institution. They receive two exam attempts per course that caused termination. Exams are announced and held within 2 months of application. Unsuccessful students get one makeup exam per failed course, conducted within 2 months after the initial exam.

nodes.title: Geçici Madde 46 – (Ek: 22/6/2000 – 4584/2 md.)
nodes.summary: Temporary Article 46 (added 22/6/2000) grants transitional rights to higher education students whose enrollment was terminated between Sept 12, 1980 and the end of 1999-2000. Key provisions include: attendance, two exams, and make-up exam rights for all courses causing termination; reinstatement upon success; attendance opportunities for practical education students; rights for students failing up to three courses in class-passing systems; one exam to improve GPA in three chosen courses; one-time attendance and exam rights plus two extra years for those exceeding maximum study periods; no mid-term requirement for affected students; protection against non-legal obstruction of rights; military service deferment and two-month post-discharge/detention application windows; rights for conservatory and external completion exam students affected by exam cancellations; and specific provisions for Gülhane Military Medical Academy students (excluding judicial/disciplinary cases) to transfer to medical faculties. All applications must be filed within two months of the law's publication.

nodes.title: Geçici Maddde 47 – (Ek: 22/6/2000 – 4584/2 md.)
nodes.summary: The text covers Temporary Articles 47-50 of a Turkish Higher Education Law. Article 47 grants re-enrollment, additional exam rights, and thesis time extensions to graduate students who lost enrollment between 1988-2000; sets foreign language exam score thresholds (50/100 for master's/PhD, 65/100 for associate professorship); removes work-duration limits for assistant professors; allows reappointment of research assistants; permits continuation for students affected by YÖK decisions; extends military service deferment; and grants return rights to students sent abroad. Article 48 cancels all disciplinary penalties and removes records for students enrolled from 1989-1990 onward. Article 49 transfers the YÖK ÖSYM Fund's assets, personnel, and liabilities to the ÖSYM Döner Sermaye İşletmesi. Article 50 provides one year of attendance and three exam chances to students who lost enrollment after June 2000, with provisions for practical courses, class-promotion failures, and GPA-related failures.

nodes.title: Temporary Provisions on Student Rights, Disciplinary Records, and ÖSYM Fund Transfer
nodes.summary: This page covers three provisions: (1) Students sent abroad for master's or doctoral studies who return to Turkey for any reason or upon expiry of their stay period, with duties terminated, are granted the right to continue studies for two (master's) or four (doctoral) semesters at YÖK-designated Turkish universities, requiring application within two months of the law's effective date. (2) Temporary Article 48 (added 22/6/2000) annuls all disciplinary penalties imposed on students enrolled in preparatory, associate, or bachelor's programs from the 1989-1990 academic year until the law's effective date, with records removed from files without requiring application. (3) Temporary Article 49 (added 21/2/2001) transfers the YÖK Student Selection and Placement Center Fund's assets, liabilities, personnel, and obligations to the ÖSYM Revolving Fund Enterprise, with initial capital of one trillion lira covered from the transferred cash balance.

nodes.title: Geçici Madde 50- (Ek: 15/3/2005-5316/1 md.)
nodes.summary: The text covers Temporary Articles 50-53 of a Turkish higher education law. Article 50 grants terminated undergraduate students (between 29.6.2000 and the law's effective date) one year of attendance and three exam rights for failed courses, with provisions for practical education, class promotion, GPA failures, graduation, maximum study duration, level determination exams, military service, and detention cases; application within two months. Article 51 extends similar rights to terminated graduate students: two exam rights for failed courses/qualification, thesis preparation time (1 year master's, 2 years doctoral), foreign language exam retakes, and art/medical specialization failures; two-month application deadline. Article 52 protects partial-status staff from reclaiming position/duty allowances paid before 15/3/2004 and mandates payment of unpaid allowances for 15/1/2003–14/3/2004. Article 53 addresses those sent abroad or to other universities for graduate education who could not complete studies within the required period.

nodes.title: Temporary Provisions on Student Rights and Staff Allowances
nodes.summary: This page covers temporary provisions of Law 2547 (Higher Education Law). It grants students who exceeded maximum study periods one year to complete courses and exams; failed level-determination exam takers an extra exam; and addresses military service, detention, and observation cases with two-month application windows. Geçici Madde 51 (2005) provides postgraduate students who lost enrollment between June 2000 and the law's effective date two exam chances for failed courses, one year (master's) or two years (PhD) for thesis preparation, and two foreign language exam attempts. It also grants two exam chances for art proficiency and medical specialization failures. Geçici Madde 52 (2006) protects part-time staff's position and duty allowances paid before March 2004 from reclamation, mandates refunds if reclaimed, and requires payment of unpaid allowances for the January 2003–March 2004 period.

nodes.title: Geçici Madde 53- (Ek: 29/6/2006-5535-2 md.)
key_items: b) Eğitimin herhangi bir aşamasında, her ne sebeple olursa olsun Türkiye’ye çağrılmış
nodes.summary: The text covers Temporary Articles 53–84 and final provisions of Turkey's Higher Education Law (No. 2547). Key topics include: reinstatement and reassignment rights for graduate students sent abroad/domestically who failed to complete studies, with mandatory service and debt provisions (Art. 53); debt forgiveness for deceased students (Art. 54); retirement age and doçentlik rules (Art. 55); comprehensive reinstatement rights for students terminated at all levels with specific exam, thesis, and military service provisions (Art. 56); part-time to full-time conversion (Art. 57); multiple reinstatement provisions for different periods (Arts. 58, 63, 68, 78, 83); student fee refunds (Arts. 60, 71); secondary education score calculations (Arts. 61–62); medical/dental faculty health center debt settlements (Arts. 66, 75, 79); mandatory industry training for science/engineering students (Art. 74); foundation university hospital requirements (Art. 82); YÖK specialist appointments (Art. 76); research assistant reassignments (Arts. 65, 84); and entry-into-force/execution provisions.

This section covers Additional Article 46 and the full set of Temporary Provisions (Articles 1–84) of Turkey's Higher Education Law (No. 2547). It addresses: part-time assignment of foreign doctoral researchers; YÖK establishment, council dissolution, and member renewal; academic title applications and exam extensions; salary and personnel protections for METU, Boğaziçi, and other institutions; civil servant status conversion; student re-enrollment and exam rights across multiple periods (1963–2006); graduate student reinstatement and thesis extensions; Gülhane Military Medical Academy student transfers; disciplinary record cancellations; ÖSYM fund transfer; part-time to full-time staff conversion; fee waivers and refunds; faculty retirement age adjustments; mandatory industry training; foundation university hospital requirements; YÖK specialist appointments; research assistant reassignments; debt forgiveness; and final entry-into-force and execution provisions.

summary: This section covers supplementary and temporary provisions of Turkey's Higher Education Law (No. 2547). Ek Madde 39 permits state universities to establish academic units and social facilities abroad. Ek Madde 40 mandates electronic accessibility of postgraduate theses via YÖK's National Thesis Center. Ek Madde 41 establishes the HMG and İYÖS exams as prerequisites for legal careers, detailing eligibility, subjects, frequency, ÖSYM administration, and regulatory oversight. Ek Madde 42 requires foundation universities to transfer 2% of student revenue as an education-completion guarantee. Ek Madde 43 authorizes YÖK to establish joint R&D centers. Ek Madde 44 directs 80% of open education revolving fund surpluses to YÖK for doctoral researcher training and scholarships. Ek Madde 45 provides Treasury budget support to state university medical/dental faculties with low debt coverage ratios. Ek Madde 46 addresses part-time assignment of foreign doctoral researchers. Temporary Provisions (Articles 1–84) cover personnel conversions, student re-enrollment rights, institutional protections, fee waivers, retirement adjustments, and final execution provisions.

title: 4/11/1981 TARİHLİ 2547 SAYILI ANA KANUNA İŞLENEMEYEN HÜKÜMLER
summary: The text lists temporary provisions (geçici maddeler) from various Turkish laws and decrees (1982–2001) that could not be incorporated into the Higher Education Law No. 2547. It covers: transitional rules for ongoing legal cases and YÖK procurement exemptions (Law 2653); student re-examination rights, faculty status changes, cadre transfers, and temporary staff provisions (Law 2880); re-examination rights for students failing one or three courses (Law 3248); a repealed decree (KHK 292); YÖK board election and appointment procedures (KHK 301); continuation of decree-making authority (Laws 3589, 3614); removal of dress-code penalties and management restrictions (Law 3670); two provisions annulled by the Constitutional Court (Laws 3708, 4498); rector election timelines and transitions (Law 3826); and a one-year deadline for issuing implementing regulations (Law 4702).

title: 2547 SAYILI KANUNDA EK VE DEĞİŞİKLİK YAPAN MEVZUATIN YÜRÜRLÜKTEN KALDIRDIĞI KANUN VE HÜKÜMLERİ GÖSTERİR LİSTE
summary: The text contains two comprehensive legal lists related to Turkey's Law No. 2547 (Higher Education Law). The first list identifies specific articles and provisions from various laws (including Laws 657, 241, 2333, 5434, and 292) that were repealed by amendments to Law 2547, along with the dates and numbers of the repealing legislation (KHK-243, KHK-260, and laws from 1986–1996). The second list is a detailed table showing the effective dates of all legislation (laws and presidential decrees numbered from 2653 to 6487, plus various KHKs) that added provisions or made amendments to Law 2547. It specifies which particular articles, supplementary articles, and temporary provisions of each amending law entered into force on different dates, spanning from April 1982 through June 2013. Some provisions had staggered effective dates, with certain articles taking effect on publication, the following month, or specific dates tied to academic years or compensation determinations.

title: Değiştiren Kanunun/ İptal Eden Anayasa Mahkemesi Kararının Numarası
summary: The text is a comprehensive table listing all amendments and annulments to Turkish Higher Education Law No. 2547, spanning from 2012 to 2020. It catalogs each amending instrument—ordinary laws (e.g., 6514, 6528, 6552, 6569, 6637, 6645, 6656, 6676, 6735, 6745, 6757, 6758, 6764, 7033, 7070, 7071, 7077, 7078, 7100, 7104, 7141, 7143, 7146, 7161, 7188, 7243), decree-laws (KHK/671, 674, 676, 678, 690, 694, 703), and Constitutional Court decisions (2012, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2019)—along with the specific articles of Law 2547 affected (including regular articles, supplementary articles, and temporary articles) and their respective effective dates, which range from 2013 to 2021.

title: Değiştiren Kanunun/
summary: The text is a tabular summary of amendments to Turkish Law No. 2547 (Higher Education Law). It lists the amending laws (Nos. 7244, 7254, 7411, 7413, 7417, 7420, 7437, 7531) and Constitutional Court decisions (with dates, case numbers, and ruling numbers from 2022–2024) that modified or annulled specific provisions. The affected articles include Supplementary Articles (Ek Madde 3, 11, 29, 31, 34, 38, 41, 42, 45, 46), Transitional Articles (Geçici Madde 80, 82, 83, 84), Article 53, 53/A, 54, and various paragraphs of Article 58. The table also specifies the effective dates of each amendment, ranging from April 2020 to November 2024, with some taking effect on fixed dates and others on dates relative to Official Gazette publication.
